<reason>Side B (PRO) built the stronger path to victory by directly embracing the proposition's trade-off ("even when transportation and parent schedules become harder") and framing the debate as an asymmetry between unadjustable adolescent biology and adjustable adult logistics. While Side A effectively raised economic costs and the bedtime compensation challenge, Side B neutralized these by arguing that (1) compensation would require a full hour of nightly bedtime delay to cancel gains—biologically unlikely given circadian delay; (2) the status quo also imposes heavy costs on hourly families through sleep-related absences and crashes; and (3) crucially, Side A's local alternatives failed to protect the early-waking teen, leaving the harmful start time intact. Side B's Rebuttal 2 decisively answered both pressure questions, and the closing crystallized the unanswered asymmetry.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 (Turn 7), where it answered A's pressure questions by arguing that bedtime compensation would require a full hour of nightly delay to negate the benefit, and that CON's alternatives leave the harmful timetable in place while the floor reaches the harm built into the schedule.</best_rebuttal>
